body.statement: The estimator in def:adjoint-covariance retains the finite-bandwidth harmonic translation score and every generated-target cross product and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). The harmonic variance and its Green cross-covariances vanish after division by \(L_n\), but retaining them makes the finite-bandwidth covariance exact. Uniform positive definiteness of \(V(P)\), covariance consistency, and \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\) imply \(\max_{1\le j\le J}\lVert(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}-V_j(P)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so the ridge is asymptotically negligible while every block inverse exists in every sample.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove normalized opposite-fold score consistency for every corrected harmonic, generated-target, coefficient, transformed-kernel, and moving-pole term.
obligation.obstruction: Cross-fitting supplies a conditional law of large numbers only after the singular pilot score is shown close to its population counterpart at the logarithmic norm scale.
obligation.attempted: The corrected harmonic adjoints and the conditional fourth-moment variance reduction are explicit; the singular pilot comparison is still missing.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditioning on the training folds makes the evaluation-fold observations independent.  The fourth-moment envelope would imply, entrywise,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\!\left[
L_n^{-1}\frac n{n_g}\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})
\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})^{\mathsf T}
\ \middle|\ \text{training folds}\right]
\leq\frac{C}{nh_n^2L_n^2}=o(1).
\]
The corrected derivative now identifies the harmonic adjoints.  Covariance consistency still requires the unproved normalized \(L^2(P_g)\) stability of the full opposite-fold score under coefficient, transformed-kernel, and pole estimation.
